We use the following pruning lemma.

Lemma. Let r≥2. From any 2r^2−3r+2 positive numbers one can select r numbers so that none of the selected numbers is a sum of between 2 and r selected numbers, repetitions allowed.

To prove it, list the numbers in increasing order and perform the usual descending greedy pruning. Whenever a number is selected, delete every number which would make a forbidden equality with the numbers already selected. Positivity implies that, for each of the at most r−1 possible numbers of summands already present, the largest summand uniquely identifies the equality and hence the deleted numbers can be charged to distinct positions among the selected list. There are at most r−1 charges of the first kind and at most r charges of the second kind, so one selection deletes at most 2r−1 numbers in total. If the procedure stopped with fewer than r selected numbers, at most

(2r−1)(r−1)=2r^2−3r+1

numbers would have been removed. This is smaller than 2r^2−3r+2, a contradiction. Therefore r numbers are selected, and the deletion rule ensures the stated property.

Taking r=n gives a subset A of M with n elements. By the lemma, for every k with 2≤k≤n, no sum of k (not necessarily distinct) elements of A belongs to A.

The construction deletes precisely every candidate that would violate the required condition, so the resulting B has the lemma’s property. ∎
